# Event-buffer timing study (OR-R14, open decision Q2)

*Generated by `sim/event_timing/compare.py` on 2026-09-28 17:13 UTC. Question and method: [README](../event_timing/README.md). Morpho lets `price()` drop at most 17.29% in one step (LLTV 77%, LIF 1.07411), i.e. a stock move of up to **+20.9%** in one round.*

## 1. Single-jump model over 10 years of prints

Assumes the whole close → next-open gap arrives in **one** round (the worst case the question was posed for). Release-on-round is exposed only when `endTs` is wrong (early or late); p_err is that probability.

| Stock | Prints | Event buffer | Worst up gap | Release on time: worst / over bound | Early or late: worst / over bound | Anchored: worst / over bound | Release-on-round expected prints over bound per 10y at p_err = 0% / 10% / 25% / 50% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NVDA | 40 | 10% | +26.1% (2023-05-24) | +14.7% / 0 | +26.1% / 1 | +14.7% / 0 | 0.00 / 0.10 / 0.25 / 0.50 |
| AAPL | 40 | 8% | +7.9% (2024-05-02) | -0.1% / 0 | +7.9% / 0 | +0.0% / 0 | 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 / 0.00 |

## 2. What the 24/5 feed does at a print (onchain)

The two prints inside the onchain history, against the release time the calendar uses for `endTs`.

| Print | `endTs` | Last round before | First round at/after | Delay | First step | Rounds in 3h | Largest single step | Move over 3h (max up / max down) | Buffer released early? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AAPL | 2026-07-30 16:30 ET | 16:02:04 | 16:30:34 | 34 s | -1.27% | 22 | 1.32% | -1.3% / -8.5% | no |
| NVDA | 2026-08-26 16:20 ET | 16:19:36 | 16:20:36 | 36 s | -1.41% | 29 | 1.41% | +4.6% / -2.8% | no |

**Reading.** The Chainlink 24/5 feed prices after-hours trading on a 0.5% deviation: the result reaches `price()` as dozens of ≤ 1.5% steps within minutes of the release, not as one round at the next open. Both observed prints released on time (first post-print round 30–36 s after `endTs`, no pre-print round at or after `endTs`). Over all onchain rounds (June–September 2026) the largest single step is 1.52% ([mainnet-params.md](mainnet-params.md) §4).

## 3. Conclusion (Q2)

**Keep release-on-round** (the built design); do not propose the anchored oracle. Reasons:

1. Even in the single-jump worst case, no 10y print breaches the Morpho bound when `endTs` is right (NVDA: 0 of 40, AAPL: 0 of 40); only a timing error could, and only for gaps above +20.9% (worst: +26.1%).

2. The feed is 24/5: prints arrive as small steps (≤ 1.5% observed), so the single-jump case does not occur on this feed while it is publishing; the buffer's job at a print is to cover the minutes of repricing, which the 0.5%-deviation rounds already bound.

3. Timing errors are rare and visible: `endTs` = the company's announced release minute (A10, confirmed dates only; 2 of 2 onchain prints on time). The calendar-push runbook and MON-R13 cover changes.

4. Anchored costs a new oracle version, new Morpho markets and a liquidity migration for a risk the data does not show.

**Residual risk and the trigger to revisit:** a print while the feed is *not* publishing (a weekend or holiday release, or a feed outage across the release) would arrive as one step at the reopen. Both are covered by the weekend buffer and the guard (`STALE`), and neither has happened for NVDA/AAPL in 10 years (every print is a weekday after the close). Revisit if a company moves its release outside feed hours or if a print ever reaches `price()` in one step above 5%.

**Owner action:** the risk owner confirms this conclusion in [risk-signoff.md](../../docs/owner-actions/risk-signoff.md) (Q2).
